quantum_entanglement.goal: Find the probability that two polarisation-entangled photons in the state |Φ+> give the same result when the two polarisers are set at an angle θ to each other.

vars.θ: angle between the two polariser axes (radians)

quantum_entanglement.method: For |Φ+> the joint amplitude for matching outcomes depends only on the relative angle and is the projection cos θ of one axis on the other; square the amplitude to get a probability (Malus-like law for the pair).

cryogenics.goal: Find the best possible coefficient of performance of a refrigerator pulling heat out of liquid helium at Tc and dumping it into a room at Th.
cryogenics.method: A reversible (Carnot) cycle moves heat Qc with zero total entropy change, so Qc/Tc = Qh/Th; the work is Qh - Qc and the COP is heat removed per unit work.

formal_logic.goal: Show how many distinct Boolean functions (truth tables) exist on n propositional variables, with n = 3.
formal_logic.method: A truth table on n variables has 2^n rows, and each row can independently be assigned true or false, so count the ways to fill 2^n rows with two values.

antimatter.goal: Find the angular cyclotron frequency of an antiproton held in a Penning trap with magnetic field B.
antimatter.method: Set the magnetic Lorentz force qvB equal to the centripetal force mv^2/r; the speed cancels when you form ω = v/r, so the frequency is independent of orbit size.

tachyonics.goal: Find the squared speed (in units of c²) of a tachyon whose imaginary-mass scale divided by its energy is r = |μ|c²/E = 0.75.

vars.r: ratio |μ|c²/E of the tachyon mass scale to its energy

tachyonics.method: Put an imaginary mass m = iμ into E² = p²c² + m²c⁴ to get p²c² = E² + μ²c⁴, and use v = pc²/E; as E grows the ratio shrinks and v falls toward c.

artificial_intelligence.goal: Find the cross-entropy loss of a neural network that assigns probability p to the correct class.

vars.p: probability the network gives to the correct answer

artificial_intelligence.method: Cross-entropy sums -target·ln(prediction) over classes; with a one-hot target only the correct class survives.

calculus.goal: Find the slope of y = x^n at the point x, for n = 3 and x = 2.

vars.x: point where the derivative is taken

calculus.method: Expand (x+h)^n with the binomial theorem, subtract x^n, divide by h and let h go to 0; only the term linear in h survives.

electrochemistry.goal: Find the Gibbs free energy change of a Daniell cell (Zn/Cu) per mole of reaction from its cell voltage.
electrochemistry.method: The maximum electrical work is charge times voltage; one mole of reaction moves nF coulombs, and a spontaneous cell has negative ΔG.

nanotechnology.goal: Find how many assemblers exist after t hours if one self-replicating assembler copies itself every τ hours.
nanotechnology.method: Every replication cycle doubles the population, and t/τ cycles fit into the elapsed time.

quantum_chemistry.goal: Find the energy of the n = 2 level of the hydrogen atom from the Schrödinger equation.
quantum_chemistry.method: Solving the Schrödinger equation for the Coulomb potential gives bound levels scaling as the inverse square of the principal quantum number, with the Rydberg energy 13.6 eV as the scale.

annihilation_power.goal: Find the energy released when 1 μg of antimatter annihilates with the same mass of matter in a reactor of efficiency η.
annihilation_power.method: Annihilation converts the rest mass of both particle and antiparticle into energy via E = mc², so the total mass converted is twice the antimatter mass.

number_theory.goal: Find the approximate number of primes below one million using the prime number theorem.
number_theory.method: The density of primes near x is about 1/ln x (Gauss), so the count up to x is roughly x times that density.

genomics.goal: Find the sequencing coverage (Lander-Waterman) of a human genome sequenced with N reads of length L.
genomics.method: Total sequenced bases spread over the genome give the average number of times each base is read.

standard_model.goal: Find the W boson mass from the weak coupling g and the Higgs vacuum expectation value v.
standard_model.method: Expanding the Higgs kinetic term around its vacuum value v gives a mass term for the W, with mass proportional to the coupling times v (with a factor of one half).

singularity_physics.goal: Find the Schwarzschild (event-horizon) radius of a black hole of one solar mass.
singularity_physics.method: Set the Newtonian escape velocity sqrt(2GM/r) equal to c and solve for r; the exact general-relativistic result happens to agree.

penrose_process.goal: Find the maximum energy extractable by the Penrose process from a rotating black hole of mass M and horizon area A (units G = c = 1).
penrose_process.method: Horizon area can never decrease, so the irreducible mass sqrt(A/16π) cannot be extracted; everything above it is rotational energy available to the ergosphere.

research_synthesis.goal: Find the time a learning machine needs for its n-th study task under a power-law learning curve (Wright's law).
research_synthesis.method: Each doubling of experience cuts the time by a constant factor (b = 0.322 means 80% per doubling); a constant factor per doubling is a power law in n.

extremophiles.goal: Find the rate constant of an enzyme-catalysed reaction in a hyperthermophile living at 121 °C, using the Arrhenius law.
extremophiles.method: Only molecules with energy above the barrier react, and the Boltzmann fraction of those is exp(-Ea/RT); multiply by the attempt frequency.

white_holes.goal: Find the speed at which matter is ejected from a white hole as it passes radius r (the time reverse of infall from rest at infinity).
white_holes.method: Reverse the free-fall solution: an object falling from rest at infinity reaches v = sqrt(2GM/r), and writing 2GM = rs c² gives a form in units of c that hits c exactly at the horizon.

hyperdimensional_geometry.goal: Find the hypervolume of a 4-dimensional ball of radius r.
hyperdimensional_geometry.method: The n-ball volume is π^(n/2) r^n / Γ(n/2 + 1); for n = 4 the Gamma function is 2! = 2. Equivalently integrate the 3-ball volume over slices.

compact_stars.goal: Find the characteristic (spin-down) age in years of a pulsar with period P and period derivative Pd (the Crab pulsar).
compact_stars.method: Magnetic dipole braking makes P·dP/dt constant; integrating from a much shorter initial period gives an age of P/(2 dP/dt) seconds, then divide by the seconds in a year.

fractional_distillation.goal: Find the minimum number of theoretical stages in the Fractionation Spire (Fenske equation) to reach a separation factor S with relative volatility α.

vars.α: relative volatility of the two components

fractional_distillation.method: At total reflux each equilibrium stage multiplies the light/heavy ratio by α, so N stages give α^N = S; take logarithms.

brane_cosmology.goal: Find the Randall-Sundrum warp factor that suppresses energies on our brane relative to the hidden brane.

vars.r: radius of the extra dimension (units of 1/k scale)

brane_cosmology.method: In the warped metric ds² = e^(-2k|y|)ημν dx dx - dy², masses scale with the square root of the warp, e^(-k|y|), evaluated at the second brane y = πr.

compactification.goal: Find the energy of the n-th Kaluza-Klein excitation of a field on an extra dimension curled into a circle of radius R.
compactification.method: A wave on a circle must fit a whole number of wavelengths, so momentum around the extra dimension is quantised as nħ/R; seen from 4D, that momentum times c appears as rest energy.

category_theory.goal: Show how many morphisms A×B → C exist in the category of finite sets by counting maps A → C^B (currying, the exponential adjunction), with |A| = 2, |B| = 3, |C| = 2.
category_theory.method: The exponential object C^B has |C|^|B| elements (all functions B → C), and Hom(A×B, C) ≅ Hom(A, C^B) because a two-argument map is a map returning a one-argument map.

m_theory.goal: Find the 11-dimensional Planck length of M-theory from the string coupling gs and string length ls.
m_theory.method: Matching the 10D Newton constant (∝ gs² ls⁸) to the 11D one (∝ l11⁹) compactified on a circle of radius R11 = gs ls gives l11⁹ = gs³ ls⁹.

traversable_wormholes.goal: Find the (negative) energy density needed at the throat of an Ellis wormhole of throat radius r (units G = c = 1).
traversable_wormholes.method: Insert the Ellis metric into Einstein's equations G = 8πT; the flare-out condition at the throat forces an energy density whose magnitude scales like the inverse square of the throat radius, and it must be negative (exotic matter).

dark_energy.goal: Find the Hubble rate when the universe was half its present size (scale factor a), with matter and dark energy (cosmological constant).
dark_energy.method: The Friedmann equation sets H² proportional to total density; matter dilutes with volume (a^-3) while vacuum energy stays constant.

causality_violation.goal: Find the time interval, in a frame moving at speed v (Lorentz factor γ), between sending and receiving a faster-than-light signal - negative means it arrives before it was sent (units c = 1).

vars.γ: Lorentz factor of the moving frame
vars.Δt: time between emission and reception in the rest frame

causality_violation.method: Apply the Lorentz transformation for time; when the signal speed Δx/Δt exceeds 1/v the bracket turns negative, which is how superluminal signals create closed causal loops.

directed_evolution.goal: Find the probability that a single mutant with selective advantage s takes over a population of N (Moran process, small s).
directed_evolution.method: The mutant count is a biased random walk; the gambler's-ruin result (1 - 1/r)/(1 - 1/r^N) with r = 1 + s becomes this for small s - drift wins in small populations, selection in large ones.

matrioshka_brain.goal: Find the equilibrium temperature of the outermost Matrioshka shell (area A = 4πR² at 1 AU) around a star of luminosity L, which sets the Landauer cost per bit of the whole brain.
matrioshka_brain.method: In steady state the outer shell must radiate the star's entire luminosity to space as a blackbody emitting σT⁴ per unit area (inner shells pass their waste heat outward).

stellar_transcendence.goal: Find the ionisation ratio n_i/n_0 of hydrogen at thermal energy T = kT from the Saha equation, showing how heat strips matter of its atomic identity.
stellar_transcendence.expr: C * T ^ 1.5 * exp ( - χ / T ) / n
stellar_transcendence.method: Treat ionisation as a chemical equilibrium: the freed electron gains a thermal phase-space factor proportional to T^(3/2) but pays a Boltzmann penalty exp(-χ/kT); kT = 0.8617 eV is 10 000 K.

incompleteness.goal: Find the Gödel number of the symbol sequence with codes (a, b, c) = (3, 1, 2), using prime-power encoding.
incompleteness.method: Raise the i-th prime to the code of the i-th symbol and multiply; unique prime factorisation lets arithmetic decode the formula, so arithmetic can talk about its own proofs.

horizon_simulation.goal: Find how many bits a black hole of horizon radius r can store (Bekenstein-Hawking entropy), with r and the Planck length l in the same units.
horizon_simulation.method: The entropy is a quarter of the horizon area 4πr² in Planck units, S = A/(4 l²); divide by ln 2 to convert nats to bits.

theory_of_everything.goal: Find the inverse strong coupling at the grand-unification scale Q by running it up from μ = M_Z with the one-loop renormalisation group equation.
theory_of_everything.method: At one loop dα/d ln Q = -bα²/2π, which makes 1/α linear in ln Q; the three Standard Model couplings run toward each other at about 10^16 GeV.

omnilex.goal: Find the Bekenstein bound - the most bits any region of radius R containing energy E can hold - for a proton; the Omnilex would need this many bits per proton to simulate reality.
omnilex.method: Lower an object into a black hole: the generalised second law demands the horizon entropy gain (∝ RE) exceed the object's entropy; divide nats by ln 2 for bits.
